description: Kotlin's !in tests that a list does not hold an item, as not in does
!in tests that a string does not contain a piece of text
!in over a class tests that none of its instances equals the item
code:
class Seat
front = Seat()
[front !in Seat, 3 !in Seat]

description: A declaration written with !in stays live as its list grows
code:
xs = [1, 2]
missing = 3 !in xs
assert(missing, true)
xs.push(3)
missing

description: A class-level rule with !in marks every order whose status is not approved
code:
class Order(status):
    this.status = status
approved = ["paid"]
$Order.pending = $Order.status !in approved
first = Order("new")
second = Order("paid")
assert([first.pending, second.pending], [true, false])
approved.push("new")
[first.pending, second.pending]

description: An if condition written with !in guards its block until the name is blocked
code:
blocked = ["eve"]
user = "bob"
access = "denied"
if user !in blocked:
    access = "granted"
access

description: A lambda written with !in filters out the banned items
!in binds as tightly as < so arithmetic comes first and == after
code:
xs = [1, 2, 3]
[1 + 3 !in xs, 4 !in xs == true, 2 !in xs or 4 !in xs]

description: !in over a null collection waits for it, as not in does
code:
tags = null
untagged = "red" !in tags
assert(untagged, null)
tags = ["blue"]
untagged

description: !in over an object raises the TypeError of not in and rolls the update back
code:
items = ["a"]
absent = "b" !in items
failure = ""
try:
    items = {a: 1}
catch error:
    failure = error
[failure, items, absent]

description: A rule written with !in renders as not in when why explains it
!in works in a comprehension filter and in a quantifier condition
code:
xs = [1, 2, 3, 4]
banned = [2]
[[x for x in xs if x !in banned], all x in xs: x !in [9]]
